headline: Highest risk is medium: no direct shared-channel evidence, but docs-only pair still has plausible prompt-injection, leakage, and workflow-conflict pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is an open-source audio-speech repo with MCP/RAG tags, while agent B is Dagster with no clipboard, stdin/stdout, or file surfaces exposed. No shared channel is documented, so a direct injection path is not evidenced; the remaining pathway is unusual manual bridging or external orchestration, which keeps blast radius small.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies A's generated text into B's pipeline
IF a shared MCP or message queue is added between A and B
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces
Disable any manual copy-paste bridge between outputs and prompts
Add a provenance label to any text passed from A to B
requires-engineering: insert a sanitizer/allowlist before B ingests A output

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both profiles show network egress none and no touched data classes, and B has no filesystem read/write or API calls. A has no exposed I/O surfaces either. With no documented shared workspace or sensitive data class, leakage is not evidenced; any leak would require extra integration not present in the profiles.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem is mounted into both agents
IF either agent is later configured to handle secrets or regulated data
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory
Confirm both agents run with network egress disabled
Review mounts and remove any unintended workspace sharing
requires-engineering: add per-agent data-loss controls and audit logging

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A exposes no filesystem or git permissions in the profile, and B explicitly cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. That makes overlapping write conflict unlikely in default settings. Uncertainty remains because A's runnable surfaces are sparse and could be extended externally, so the safer choice is low rather than none.
conditions: IF A is deployed with additional write or git permissions outside the profile
IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory by an external orchestrator
mitigations: Avoid mounting the same writable directory into both agents
Check that A has no hidden write path in deployment
requires-engineering: add lock/lease coordination for any shared mutable resource

D_cascading_error.rationale: A's repo tags include agents, llms, mcp, and rag, which suggests it may produce generated content that B could consume in a pipeline. B is a data orchestrator, so if its workflow treats A output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream jobs even without direct evidence of action-taking. The interaction is inferred, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF B ingests A output as a pipeline input without validation
IF downstream Dagster jobs act on A-produced text or metadata
mitigations: Add a verification step before B consumes A output
Require schema validation on any A-produced payload
Log and review failed parses from A to B
requires-engineering: add human approval before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: No data classes are touched by either agent, no residency or retention mismatch is documented, and both profiles show no network egress. Because the compliance pathway is not evidenced and no regulated data flow is present, there is no plausible compliance breach to score here.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later introduced into either agent
IF a jurisdiction-specific retention policy is added to one agent only
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents
Document retention and residency settings before deployment
Recheck compliance if either profile gains data-handling scopes
